name: Lists
summary: Use semantic GOV.UK lists to break information into manageable chunks and communicate whether order matters.
rules: Use ul when order does not matter and ol when sequence, rank or count matters.
Apply govuk-list and add govuk-list--bullet or govuk-list--number for visible markers.
Introduce a bulleted list with a lead-in line ending in a colon; normally start each item in lowercase without a final full stop.
Use govuk-list--spaced only when longer items need extra separation.
accessibility: Keep native ul, ol and li elements so assistive technology announces list structure and item count.
Do not simulate list markers with text characters or CSS on unrelated elements.
Nested lists must reflect the actual content hierarchy.
restrictions: Do not use a list merely to align controls or create columns.
Avoid long, deeply nested lists; split or restructure the content when scanning becomes difficult.
